title: The first ten kilometres
summary: From a first 10K in March to a half marathon in September, measured one run at a time.

body: On 13 March 2026 I ran ten kilometres without stopping for the first time. I named the activity exactly what it felt like: “FIRST 10KM RUN !”. Six months later I finished the BOOM RUN half marathon, 21.42 km.
Neither run was fast. That is not the point of this page. The point is what happened in between: the boring, repeated, measurable work that engineering already taught me to trust.

body: Running is the same loop as building software: input, process, iterate, progress. The difference is that you cannot refactor your legs overnight. Progress only shows up over months, which is exactly why it is worth writing down.
